pages.title: Start here: how this workspace runs

text.text: A ten-minute tour of how the practice runs in this workspace. Share it with every therapist and the front desk.
: what you offer, the price and length, how many you gave, and how many members are active.
: membership, usual session, health cautions, pressure, areas to avoid, intake date and banked sessions.
: each session with therapist, room, focus areas, SOAP notes, price and tip.
: session payments, monthly member charges, gift cards and refunds.
A session from booking to notes
The front desk books the session and room, and sends the intake form for first visits.
The therapist reads the client card before the session.
After the session, write the SOAP notes, press
Every morning: Dashboard, today's sessions, failed member charges
Every afternoon: confirm tomorrow by text
Every Friday: linens and supplies count
Every month: banked sessions, no-shows, room use

Change the session menu, prices and room names to your own, and delete the sample clients once you have a dozen of your own. Type in any cell or drag cards between columns; every total updates by itself.
Health history and session notes are marked confidential. Only the team sees them, and only to care for the client. Never paste them into messages or emails.
A member pays monthly for one session. If they skip a month, the session is banked for three months.
on the client card shows how many they have; the Dashboard lists members with banked sessions so the front desk can invite them in before any expire. Paused members are not charged.
Appointments this week, no-shows and payments.
Good notes keep clients safe and make every therapist in the practice as good as the one who knows the client best. Write them in plain words, the same way every time.
Send the intake form when the client books. It asks about health conditions, medications, surgeries, pregnancy, allergies to oils or scents, and what they want from the session.
Read it before they arrive. Copy anything that changes how you work into
When in doubt about a condition, ask the client to check with their doctor before deep work. Never diagnose.
At the start of each session
Ask what has changed since last time: new injuries, medications, pregnancy, how they felt after the last session
Agree the focus areas and the pressure, and remind them they can change it at any time
Confirm any area they do not want touched
: where it hurts, how long, what makes it worse.
: tight areas, trigger points, range of motion, skin issues you noticed.
A, what you did and how it went
: techniques, how the tissue responded, how they felt after.
: home stretches, how soon to come back, anything to try next time.
Keep it short and factual. Notes can be read by the client and, in some cases, by insurers or lawyers.

A runner books a 90 minute session for a tight hamstring. The therapist writes: S, tight after a long run; O, trigger points mid-hamstring and tight hip flexors; A, eased with cross-fiber and stretching, no pain after; P, stretch daily, back in three weeks. Next visit, a different therapist reads it and starts in the same place.
when the client tells you something new. Re-sign the intake once a year, or at once after surgery or pregnancy.
Health details are confidential. Talk about clients only with the team, only when it helps the client, and never in the waiting area.
An empty room is income you never get back. Reminders and a clear, kind cancellation policy cut no-shows to almost nothing.
A text when the session is booked, with the date, time, therapist and address.
A reminder two days before, asking them to reply to confirm.
A short message the morning of the session with parking tips for first visits.
Ask for at least 24 hours' notice. Write the policy on the booking page and the intake form.
A late cancellation or no-show may be charged a part of the session, at your discretion.
Members who no-show lose that month's session unless they reschedule within the week.
Call or text kindly the same day: "We missed you today. Is everything all right? Shall I find you another time?"
After two no-shows the card says
: take a card at booking from then on.
Keep a short list of clients who want a sooner time. When a session is cancelled, text the list; the first to reply gets the room.
Members are charged monthly on their card on file. If a charge fails, the payment shows
on the Dashboard: call the member that day.
Unused sessions are banked for three months; update
when a month passes without a visit, and remind the member before one expires.
A member who wants a break can be set to
for up to two months rather than cancelling.
Waiting list ready for any cancellation

A member's monthly charge fails on Monday. The front desk calls; her card expired. She updates it on the phone, the charge goes through, and while on the call she books her banked session for Thursday.
Clients judge a practice by the room before the first touch: clean linens, the right temperature, quiet, and nothing out of place.
Fresh face cradle cover, sheets and blanket; table warmer on ten minutes before
Room at a comfortable temperature, lights dimmed, music low
Oils and lotions checked against the client's allergies; unscented for clients who ask
Bolsters and, for prenatal, side-lying pillows ready
Hands washed, nails short, no strong perfume
Strip the table into the laundry bin, never on the floor
Wipe the table, face cradle, bolsters, door handles and the bottle pumps
Remake the table and reset the room
Allow 15 minutes between sessions in the same room; book rooms with that gap
Wash sheets hot with an unscented detergent; add an oil-removing booster weekly so oil does not build up and go rancid.
Dry completely and store in a closed cabinet.
Count sets every Friday. Each room needs at least three sets per session booked that day.
column on each session so two therapists never book the same room. The Dashboard shows how much each room is used; a room used far less than the others may be a better price for a new therapist.
Oils and lotions, face cradle covers, hand soap, laundry detergent and the booster, tissues, water cups. Check them every Friday with the linens.
On Friday the front desk counts linens: the Fern room has two sets for four prenatal sessions on Saturday. Two sets are moved from storage and an extra wash runs that evening.
Oil on the floor is a slip waiting to happen. Wipe it straight away and keep a non-slip mat at the table step.
New therapists walk through this page with the owner on their first day, then reset a room on their own while the owner watches.
